fieldMarks: 8-10 in; small, chunky quail with a puffy, rounded head.
Male: bold clownish black-and-white face pattern and many white spots on a chestnut belly.
Female: pale brown and subtly marked, but has the same head shape.
behavior: Crouches motionless until nearly stepped on, then explodes into whirring flight.
Fall and winter coveys usually under ten birds, often using a very small area.
Digs in soil with its feet for bulbs (wood sorrel, nutgrass) and scratches leaf litter under oaks for insects, acorns and seeds.
Mostly resident; northern birds may move to lower elevations in winter.
habitat: Grassy oak canyons and wooded mountain slopes with bunchgrass; needs tall grass and usually oaks.
Open oak or pine-oak woodland and grassy hills with scattered trees; avoids low deserts.
range: In the United States found only in the Mexican border region of the Southwest and Texas.
